stem:
Meena wants to find out whether warm or cold conditions change the speed at which water moves up a plant stem.
She places two similar cut hibiscus twigs in glasses of red-coloured water.
Which plan is a fair test?

options.text: Put one twig in a warm room and the other in a cold room, keeping the amount of coloured water, the size of the twigs and the light the same in both.
Put a long twig in cold water and a short twig in warm water, then see which twig turns red at the top first.
Put one twig in red ink and the other in plain water, both in the same warm room, then compare the colours.
Put a rose twig in the sun and a mango twig in the shade, then measure how much water each one absorbs.

teacher.key_rationale: A fair test of temperature on water-transport speed changes only temperature; all other variables (twig size, species, water amount, light) must be controlled, which only option A does. B confounds twig length, C changes the liquid not the temperature, and D confounds plant species with location.
